# Review: Emergency Power Sequence, G-1/G-2 Paralleling and ATS-L/C/E

## Summary

The sequence does not meet the 10 s restoration requirement it states. It holds all three ATSs until both generators are paralleled. A time budget shows the problem:

- 3 s utility confirmation
- Crank and accelerate a 1500 kW diesel, roughly 6 to 8 s
- 5 s stabilization delay
- Second-generator synchronizing time

The life safety and critical branches would see roughly 15 to 25 s of outage. For a hospital Type 1 essential electrical system (NFPA 99, NFPA 110 Level 1 Type 10, NEC 517/700) this is a code non-compliance.

Other gaps:

- The PLC is a single point of failure.
- The load shed requirement has no content.
- Retransfer has no delay and no cooldown.
- Two of the three listed shutdowns are alarms only under NFPA 110 Level 1.
- Three required shutdowns are missing.

Code clause references below are from memory. The electrical engineer of record (EOR) must confirm them against the edition the AHJ has adopted.

## Findings

| ID | Location | Issue | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| R-01 | 3.2 | ATS-L and ATS-C wait for both generators to be on the bus. The 10 s Type 10 limit cannot be met (see budget above). | Transfer ATS-L and ATS-C as soon as the first generator closes to the dead bus. Transfer ATS-E only after both generators are on the bus, or after a delayed-automatic timer (NEC 517 / NFPA 99 allow delayed connection of the equipment branch). |
| R-02 | 3.1 vs 3.2 | 3.1 says "start immediately". 3.2 says start after a 3 s confirmation delay. The two statements conflict. | Use one start condition: utility loss persists for the confirmation delay in the setpoint list. |
| R-03 | 3.2 | A 3 s confirmation consumes about 30 % of the 10 s budget. | Reduce it to a ride-through value (provisional 1 s, SP-01). Make the EOR confirm the total time with the generator vendor's start-time data. |
| R-04 | 3.1 | "Utility failure" is not defined. The ATSs would transfer only on a total utility loss. A single feeder or phase loss at one ATS would not transfer it. | Make each ATS monitor its own normal source, all phases, for voltage and frequency (SP-02, SP-03). Any ATS that senses a loss sends a start signal. |
| R-05 | 3.1, 3.2 | All start and transfer logic depends on the PLC. If the PLC fails, the hospital gets no emergency power. NEC 700 does not allow this. | Hardwire the engine-start contacts from each ATS to both generator controllers. Hardwire the dead-bus first-up logic. On PLC failure, ATS-L and ATS-C transfer without the PLC (FR-EPS-030). |
| R-06 | 3.2 | Nothing prevents both generators from closing to the dead bus at the same instant. | Add a hardwired dead-bus arbitration interlock: the first breaker to close blocks the other breaker's dead-bus close. The second generator can then close only through the synchronizer. |
| R-07 | 3.2 | There is no timeout for crank, for reaching ready, or for synchronizing. If G-2 never syncs, the sequence stalls with no transfer. | Add timeouts and failure responses for each step (sequence table below). |
| R-08 | 3.3 | "Sheds load as required" cannot be tested. It gives no trigger, no load list, no priority, no restore method, and no capacity check. | Shed ATS-E first on single-generator operation, bus underfrequency, or generator overload. Never shed ATS-L or ATS-C. Confirm that the life safety plus critical demand is within one generator's rating (OI-01). |
| R-09 | 3.3 | The case where a generator trips while both are on the bus is not covered. | Add a SINGLE-GEN state with an automatic ATS-E shed. |
| R-10 | 3.4 | "Retransfer immediately" exposes patients to a second outage if the utility restoration is unstable. NFPA 110 requires an adjustable time delay on retransfer. | Add a utility-stable confirmation timer and retransfer delay (SP-11). Bypass the delay and retransfer at once if the emergency source fails during the wait. |
| R-11 | 3.4 | The ATSs retransfer simultaneously, which gives a block-load step onto the utility. | Stagger the retransfers in a defined order (SP-13). State the transition type for each ATS: open, closed, or in-phase monitored (OI-04). |
| R-12 | 3.4 | "Generators stop" with no cooldown. A hot shutdown can damage the turbochargers. | Open the generator breakers. Run the engines unloaded for the cooldown time in SP-12. Then stop. |
| R-13 | 3.5 | Low coolant temperature is an alarm under NFPA 110 Level 1 (Table 5.6.5.2), not a shutdown. As written, the PLC would trip a cold standby engine when it is needed. | Change this to an alarm only. |
| R-14 | 3.5 | A low fuel level shutdown deliberately removes hospital power before the fuel runs out. For Level 1, low main tank fuel is an alarm. | Change this to an alarm with a defined runtime remaining (SP-16). Add an operator response: call for fuel delivery. |
| R-15 | 3.5 | The required Level 1 shutdowns are missing: overcrank, overspeed, low lube oil pressure. Remote emergency stop is also missing. Generator protective relays (reverse power, overcurrent, loss of excitation) are not mentioned. | Write out the full cause-and-effect rows (below). Cover generator protection by referencing the protective relay settings study. |
| R-16 | 3.5 | High coolant temperature has no pre-alarm, so the first indication the operator gets is a trip. | Add a high-temperature pre-alarm. |
| R-17 | All | No states are defined. Test mode (NFPA 110 monthly load test), manual mode, maintenance lockout, and the "no generator available" condition are all missing. | Add an ISA-106 state table (below). |
| R-18 | All | Abnormal handling is missing: bad PV, PLC or comms loss, DC control power loss, breaker fail-to-close, ATS fail-to-transfer. | Add an abnormal handling section (below). |
| R-19 | All | No alarms are defined, and no operator interface is described. | Add an alarm list and operator interface requirements (below). |
| R-20 | All | Numbers appear in prose (3 s, 5 s, 10 s). | Move them to the setpoint list and refer to them by ID. |
| R-21 | All | There are no requirement IDs or test methods. | Use FR-EPS-NNN, and give each one a FAT/SAT test. |
| R-22 | All | Breakers and the bus have no tags. | Assign tags. Provisional tags: 52-G1, 52-G2, EB-1 (OI-06). |
| R-23 | All | STE problems: passive voice ("transfer happens"), vague terms ("as required", "immediately"), and several actions in one sentence (3.2). | Rewrite as in the proposed text below. |

## Setpoint list (provisional)

These values are for a 480 V, 60 Hz system, which is an assumption (OI-07).

| ID | Parameter | Value | Units | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SP-01 | Utility loss confirmation delay | 1 | s | Confirm (was 3) |
| SP-02 | Normal source undervoltage dropout / pickup | 85 / 90 | % nominal | Confirm |
| SP-03 | Normal source underfrequency dropout / pickup | 57 / 59 | Hz | Confirm |
| SP-04 | Generator ready: voltage / frequency | 90 / 57 | % nom / Hz | Confirm with vendor |
| SP-05 | Max time, utility loss to ATS-L and ATS-C on emergency | 10 | s | Fixed (NFPA 110 Type 10) |
| SP-06 | Cyclic crank: crank / rest / attempts | 15 / 15 / 3 | s / s / count | Confirm (NFPA 110 cyclic crank) |
| SP-07 | Second generator sync timeout | 30 | s | Confirm |
| SP-08 | Delay, second generator closed to ATS-E transfer | 5 | s | Confirm (was the 5 s stabilization) |
| SP-09 | Delayed-automatic ATS-E transfer on single generator (if capacity allows) | 60 | s | Confirm with EOR (OI-01) |
| SP-10 | Bus underfrequency shed: level / delay | 58 / 2 | Hz / s | Confirm |
| SP-11 | Utility stable before retransfer | 15 | min | Confirm with owner and AHJ |
| SP-12 | Engine unloaded cooldown | 5 | min | Confirm with vendor |
| SP-13 | Retransfer stagger (order ATS-E, ATS-C, ATS-L) | 5 | s | Confirm |
| SP-14 | Breaker fail-to-close / ATS fail-to-transfer timeout | 2 | s | Confirm |
| SP-15 | Single-generator overload shed: level / delay | 100 / 5 | % rating / s | Confirm |
| SP-16 | Low main fuel alarm | 4 | h runtime at full load | Confirm with AHJ |
| SP-17 | High coolant temperature pre-alarm / shutdown | TBD | °F | Vendor (OI-03) |
| SP-18 | Low coolant temperature alarm | TBD | °F | Vendor (OI-03) |
| SP-19 | Low lube oil pressure pre-alarm / shutdown | TBD | psig | Vendor (OI-03) |
| SP-20 | Overspeed shutdown | TBD | % rated | Vendor (OI-03) |
| SP-21 | Monthly test duration | 30 | min | Confirm (NFPA 110 monthly test) |

## Proposed replacement text, module EPS

### 3.1 States (SBC)

| State | Entry permissives | Initiator | Allowed exits | Automation level |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| STANDBY | Utility normal at all ATSs. G-1 and G-2 in AUTO. 52-G1 and 52-G2 open. | Auto (from COOLDOWN) or operator | START, TEST, MAINT | Automatic |
| START | Any ATS senses normal-source loss for SP-01 | Auto | FIRST-ON-BUS, NO-GEN, RETRANSFER (if utility returns) | Automatic |
| FIRST-ON-BUS | One generator ready (SP-04) and closed to dead bus EB-1 | Auto | PARALLEL, SINGLE-GEN, NO-GEN | Automatic |
| PARALLEL | 52-G1 and 52-G2 closed. All ATSs on emergency. | Auto | SINGLE-GEN, RETRANSFER-WAIT | Automatic |
| SINGLE-GEN | One generator on EB-1. The other generator failed to start, failed to sync, or tripped. | Auto | PARALLEL (on operator reset), NO-GEN, RETRANSFER-WAIT | Automatic shed, operator-prompted restore |
| NO-GEN | No generator available | Auto | START (on operator reset), RETRANSFER | Operator-prompted |
| RETRANSFER-WAIT | Utility normal at all ATSs for SP-11 timing | Auto | RETRANSFER, or back to the previous state if the utility fails again | Automatic |
| RETRANSFER | SP-11 expired, or the emergency source failed while the utility is normal | Auto | COOLDOWN | Automatic |
| COOLDOWN | All ATSs on normal. 52-G1 and 52-G2 open. | Auto | STANDBY, START (if the utility fails again) | Automatic |
| TEST | Operator selects TEST in STANDBY | Operator | STANDBY (operator end, or SP-21 expired), START (real utility loss) | Operator-prompted |
| MAINT | Operator places a generator in OFF or lockout | Operator | STANDBY | Manual |

### 3.2 Requirements

- FR-EPS-001: Each ATS monitors all phases of its normal source against SP-02 and SP-03. Test: inject single-phase loss at each ATS and confirm the start signal and transfer.
- FR-EPS-002: Each ATS sends a hardwired start signal to G-1 and G-2. Test: disable the PLC, open the normal source, confirm both engines crank.
- FR-EPS-003: ATS-L and ATS-C are on emergency within SP-05 of utility loss. Test: timed FAT/SAT with a recorder, 3 runs.
- FR-EPS-004: The PLC never sheds ATS-L or ATS-C. Test: force SINGLE-GEN with overload and confirm that ATS-L and ATS-C stay on emergency.
- FR-EPS-030: On PLC failure, the hardwired logic closes the first ready generator to EB-1, and ATS-L and ATS-C transfer. Test: remove PLC power, then simulate utility loss.

### 3.3 Sequence, utility loss (SqBC)

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Start the SP-01 timer at the ATS that senses the loss | Loss persists for SP-01 | SP-01 | If the utility returns, go to STANDBY. No start. |
| 2 | Send start to G-1 and G-2 | One generator ready (SP-04) | SP-06 cyclic crank | Overcrank on one generator: alarm, continue. Overcrank on both: go to NO-GEN. |
| 3 | Close the first ready breaker (52-G1 or 52-G2) to dead bus EB-1. Block the other breaker's dead-bus close. | Breaker closed | SP-14 | Fail-to-close: alarm, trip that breaker, close the other generator if it is ready |
| 4 | Transfer ATS-L and ATS-C to emergency | Both ATSs show the emergency position | SP-14 | ATS fail-to-transfer: alarm, operator uses the ATS bypass-isolation switch |
| 5 | Synchronize the second generator to EB-1 and close its breaker | Second breaker closed | SP-07 | Sync timeout: alarm, stop the second generator, go to SINGLE-GEN |
| 6 | Wait SP-08, then transfer ATS-E | ATS-E shows the emergency position | SP-14 | Fail-to-transfer: alarm. EB-1 stays in PARALLEL. |
| 7 | Hold in PARALLEL | Utility normal at all ATSs | None | Generator trip: go to SINGLE-GEN |

### 3.4 Sequence, retransfer

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Start the SP-11 timer | Utility normal for SP-11 | SP-11 | Utility fails again: reset the timer and stay on emergency. Emergency source fails: skip to step 2 at once. |
| 2 | Retransfer ATS-E, then ATS-C, then ATS-L, SP-13 apart | All ATSs show the normal position | SP-14 per ATS | Fail-to-retransfer: alarm, leave that ATS on emergency, keep generators running |
| 3 | Open 52-G1 and 52-G2 | Both open | SP-14 | Fail-to-open: alarm, prompt the operator |
| 4 | Run unloaded cooldown | SP-12 expired | SP-12 | Utility fails again: return to START step 3 |
| 5 | Stop the engines and return to STANDBY | Engines stopped, in AUTO | 60 s, confirm | Fail-to-stop: alarm, prompt the operator to use the engine control stop |

### 3.5 Load shed (cause-and-effect)

| Cause | Effect | Latched / auto-reset | Reset method |
|---|---|---|---|
| SINGLE-GEN state entered | Inhibit or shed ATS-E. Apply SP-09 delayed transfer only if the EOR confirms capacity. | Latched | Operator reset after the second generator is back in PARALLEL |
| EB-1 frequency below SP-10 | Shed ATS-E | Latched | Operator reset |
| Single-generator load above SP-15 | Shed ATS-E | Latched | Operator reset |
| PLC failure | ATS-E stays on normal, or transfers per OI-05 | n/a | Restore the PLC |

### 3.6 Engine shutdowns and alarms (NFPA 110 Level 1)

| Cause | Effect | Latched / auto-reset | Reset method |
|---|---|---|---|
| Overcrank (SP-06) | Shut down that engine and alarm | Latched | Local reset at the generator controller |
| Overspeed (SP-20) | Shut down, alarm, close the air damper if fitted | Latched | Local reset |
| Low lube oil pressure (SP-19) | Shut down and alarm. A pre-alarm comes first. | Latched | Local reset |
| High coolant temperature (SP-17) | Shut down and alarm. A pre-alarm comes first. | Latched | Local reset |
| Remote emergency stop | Shut down and alarm | Latched | Local reset after the E-stop is released |
| Low coolant temperature (SP-18) | Alarm only | Auto-reset | n/a |
| Low main fuel (SP-16) | Alarm only. Prompt: call for fuel delivery. | Auto-reset | n/a |
| Generator protective relay trip | Open that breaker and go to SINGLE-GEN | Latched | Per the relay settings study |

Generator protective relay settings belong to the protective device coordination study. Do not restate them here.

### 3.7 Abnormal handling

- **Bad PV (bus PT, utility PT):** Alarm. A bad utility signal holds the present source. A bad bus signal inhibits the PLC shed and load-add. The hardwired ATS logic stays active.
- **PLC or comms loss:** The hardwired start, dead-bus arbitration, and ATS-L/ATS-C transfer operate without the PLC (FR-EPS-030). The paralleling of the second generator stops.
- **DC control power loss:** Each generator controller has its own battery. Alarm on battery charger failure. Each breaker trip coil fail position is TBD (OI-06).
- **PLC restart:** The PLC reads the actual breaker and ATS positions and enters the matching state. It does not command a transfer on restart.
- **Fail positions:** The ATSs hold their last position on loss of control power. The generator breakers trip open on protection.

### 3.8 Operator interface

The operator sees:

- The state of the module.
- Each ATS position.
- Each breaker position.
- Each generator ready, running, alarm, and shutdown status.
- Each active timer with the time remaining.

The operator can:

- Start TEST.
- Reset the latched sheds.
- Bypass the retransfer delay. This needs confirmation.

The operator is prompted to:

- Call for fuel.
- Reset after SINGLE-GEN.
- Use the bypass-isolation switch after an ATS fail-to-transfer.

Operations must sign off on the states and prompts (OI-08).
